display.title: Episode 177: King David, the Fly and the Spider (Rosh Chodesh Sivan)
display.summary_short: On Rosh Chodesh Sivan Uncle Yossi tells why children are the Torah's guarantors, a first-grade class sings for Shavuos, and Dovid HaMelech is saved by a fly and a spider.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5745, five days before Shavuos. Uncle Yossi gives the dates of Yom Tov and tells every family, down to babies in carriages, to be in shul to hear the Aseres HaDibros. He retells the Midrash: when Moshe Rabbeinu offered the elders and the yeshiva students as guarantors for the Torah, Hashem refused, until Moshe heard little children singing the Aleph-Beis and Hashem accepted them. Listeners are reminded of the Shavuos points in the Tzivos Hashem newsletter. A first-grade class from a Crown Heights yeshiva recites the Shema and sings a Yiddish song about Shavuos. Story time honors the yahrzeit of Dovid HaMelech on Shavuos. Hiding from Shaul's soldiers, David wonders why Hashem made flies; a buzzing fly wakes him just in time to escape. Later he wonders about spiders, and a spider's web across a cave mouth convinces the soldiers that no one is inside. Uncle Yossi closes with saying Tehillim, achdus at Matan Torah, and the campaign to write a letter in a new Sefer Torah.
display.lesson: Everything Hashem created has a purpose, and children learning Torah are the guarantee that the Torah will last forever.

date.note: 'Today is Rosh Chodesh Sivan'; Shavuos on Sunday 26 and Monday 27 May. Weekly estimate was 3 weeks late.

advisories.note: Soldiers hunt David from cave to cave; he escapes each time.
